objects.original: Continuous real weights, integrable density and signed dyadic cell masses.
objects.reconstructed: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. For n in N put t[n,i]=i*T/2^n for i=0,...,2^n, and Delta_i^n Z=Z(t[n,i+1])-Z(t[n,i]). Define P_b(t)=integral 1_{s<min(t,T)}*b(s)d lambda_T(s).
objects.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/DyadicWeightedLimits.lean:14; The local t,P,L,V,S definitions retain the actual masses and prefix primitive.

domains.original: Positive nonnegative-real horizon; dyadic grids; a cofinal map sigma:N→N.
domains.reconstructed: T>0 in R_+; w,b:R_+->R; z_n:{0,...,2^n-1}->R for every n in N; sigma:N->N.
domains.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/DyadicWeightedLimits.lean:14; hT, z, sigma and regularGridTimes use exactly the positive dyadic horizon.

quantifiers.original: For all data; one total-absolute-mass bound along sigma; every fixed dyadic prefix converges; then weighted sums converge.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universally T,hT,w,b,hw,hb,z,sigma,hSigma,hVar. hVar has order exists real M, forall n, sum_i |z_{sigma(n),i}|<=M. Then assume for every m and k in {0,...,2^m}, convergence of the prefix sums along n; conclude convergence of the weighted sums along n.
quantifiers.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/DyadicWeightedLimits.lean:14; hVar is exists M then forall n; hPrefix is forall m,k before the limit; no monotonicity of sigma.

assumptions.original: w continuous on [0,T]; b time-integrable; sigma→infinity; uniformly bounded sum |z| and the specified prefix limits.
assumptions.reconstructed: w is continuous on [0,T], b is lambda_T-integrable, sigma(n)->infinity (no monotonicity or injectivity required), and the total absolute sums sum_i |z_{sigma(n),i}| have one common finite real upper bound M. For every fixed m,k, sum_i 1_{t[sigma(n),i+1]<=t[m,k]}*z_{sigma(n),i} tends to P_b(t[m,k]).
assumptions.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/DyadicWeightedLimits.lean:14; hw,hb,hSigma,hVar,hPrefix are precisely the mathematical premises.

conclusion.original: Sum of left-endpoint weights times masses converges to integral w b.
conclusion.reconstructed: As n->infinity, sum_i w(t[sigma(n),i])*z_{sigma(n),i} tends in R to integral_0^T w(s)*b(s)ds.
conclusion.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/DyadicWeightedLimits.lean:14; hV takes finite prefix limits; hL is the weighted-prefix theorem; hApprox and the final triangle prove the stated limit.

scopes.original: Deterministic scalar convergence along sigma; fixed prefix nodes, not uniform in nodes.
scopes.reconstructed: Deterministic scalar convergence, with hypotheses at each fixed dyadic prefix endpoint. It does not assert uniform convergence of all prefixes. The prefix definition uses s<min(t,T), whereas the discrete cutoff uses right endpoint<=t[m,k]. All weight evaluations are at left endpoints. Bounds and convergence are only along sigma.
scopes.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/DyadicWeightedLimits.lean:14; The fine/coarse comparison is only eventual, using sigma.eventually(eventually_ge_atTop m).

constant_dependencies.original: One finite mass bound independent of sequence index; no rate.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: M is existential after z,sigma and may depend on all prior data; it is independent of n. No rate constant is concluded.
constant_dependencies.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/DyadicWeightedLimits.lean:14; C=max M 1 is internal proof bookkeeping and does not add a source premise.
